questions.text: What does a computer primarily process?
questions.explanation: A computer processes data to produce useful information.

questions.text: Who is widely regarded as the father of the computer?
questions.explanation: Charles Babbage designed the Analytical Engine, the first general-purpose computer concept.

questions.text: What does the acronym CPU stand for in full?
questions.explanation: CPU stands for Central Processing Unit, the brain of the computer.

questions.text: What does the acronym RAM stand for in full?
questions.explanation: RAM stands for Random Access Memory, a volatile memory used for temporary data storage.

questions.text: What does the acronym ROM stand for in full?
questions.explanation: ROM stands for Read Only Memory, which stores permanent data.

questions.text: Which of the following is an input device?
questions.explanation: A keyboard is an input device used to enter data into a computer.

questions.text: Which of the following is an output device?
questions.explanation: A monitor is an output device that displays visual information.

questions.text: How many bits are there in one byte?
questions.explanation: One byte consists of 8 bits.

questions.text: What is the base of the binary number system?
questions.explanation: The binary number system has a base of 2, using only 0 and 1.

questions.text: Which of the following best describes An AND gate outputs 1 only when?
questions.explanation: An AND gate outputs 1 only when all inputs are 1.

questions.text: What is the value or meaning of the Internet in mathematics?
questions.explanation: The Internet is a global system of interconnected computer networks.

questions.text: What is the difference between data and information?
options: Data is raw facts; information is processed data
questions.explanation: Data refers to raw, unprocessed facts; information is data that has been processed to be meaningful.

questions.text: Which generation of computers used transistors?
questions.explanation: Second-generation computers (1959-1965) used transistors instead of vacuum tubes.

questions.text: What is the value or meaning of volatile memory in mathematics?
options: Memory that retains data when power is off
Memory that loses data when power is off
questions.explanation: Volatile memory loses its data when the computer is powered off, e.g. RAM.

questions.text: Which of the following is a secondary storage device?
questions.explanation: A hard disk is a secondary storage device for permanent data storage.

questions.text: What does the acronym HTML stand for in full?
questions.explanation: HTML stands for HyperText Markup Language, used to create web pages.

questions.text: What is the value or meaning of an operating system in mathematics?
options: A program that manages computer resources
questions.explanation: An operating system manages hardware and software resources of a computer.

questions.text: Which of the following is an example of an operating system?
questions.explanation: Linux is an open-source operating system.

questions.text: What is the binary equivalent of decimal 10?
questions.explanation: Decimal 10 = 8+2 = 1010 in binary.

questions.text: Which input device is used to scan printed text into a computer?
questions.explanation: A scanner converts printed documents into digital images for the computer.

questions.text: What does the acronym LAN stand for in full?
questions.explanation: LAN stands for Local Area Network, connecting devices within a limited area.

questions.text: What is the primary function of an OR gate?
options: Outputs 1 only when all inputs are 1
Outputs 1 when at least one input is 1
questions.explanation: An OR gate outputs 1 when at least one of its inputs is 1.

questions.text: Which of the following is application software?
questions.explanation: Microsoft Excel is application software used for spreadsheets.

questions.text: What is the value or meaning of the purpose of a BIOS in mathematics?
options: Perform POST and initialise hardware during booting
questions.explanation: BIOS performs the Power-On Self-Test and initialises hardware during the boot process.

questions.text: How many kilobytes (KB) are in one megabyte (MB)?
What does the acronym URL stand for in full?
questions.explanation: URL stands for Uniform Resource Locator, the address of a web resource.

questions.text: What is the value or meaning of the full meaning of ICT in mathematics?
questions.explanation: ICT stands for Information and Communication Technology.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a storage device?
questions.explanation: RAM is primary memory, not a storage device; it is volatile.

questions.text: What is the value or meaning of cache memory in mathematics?
options: A high-speed memory between CPU and RAM
questions.explanation: Cache memory is a small, very fast memory located between the CPU and RAM to speed up processing.

questions.text: What is the base of the hexadecimal number system?
questions.explanation: The hexadecimal number system uses base 16 (digits 0-9 and letters A-F).

questions.text: Which of the following best describes A NOT gate is also known as?
questions.explanation: A NOT gate inverts the input signal, so it is also called an inverter.

questions.text: Which protocol is used to send emails?
questions.explanation: SMTP (Simple Mail Transfer Protocol) is used to send emails.

questions.text: What is the value or meaning of an algorithm in mathematics?
options: A step-by-step procedure to solve a problem
questions.explanation: An algorithm is a finite set of step-by-step instructions to solve a problem.

questions.text: In a flowchart, a diamond shape represents:
questions.explanation: A diamond shape in a flowchart represents a decision point.

questions.text: What does the acronym WAN stand for in full?
questions.explanation: WAN stands for Wide Area Network, covering a large geographical area.

questions.text: What is the decimal equivalent of binary 1101?
questions.explanation: 1101 in binary = 8+4+0+1 = 13 in decimal.

questions.text: Which of the following is a network topology?
questions.explanation: Star topology is a common network layout where all nodes connect to a central hub.

questions.text: What is the value or meaning of the function of a mouse in mathematics?
questions.explanation: A mouse is a pointing input device used to interact with a GUI.

questions.text: Which of the following best describes a computer virus?
options: A malicious program that replicates itself
questions.explanation: A computer virus is a malicious software designed to replicate and spread.

questions.text: What does the acronym ISP stand for in full?
questions.explanation: ISP stands for Internet Service Provider, a company that provides Internet access.

questions.text: Which generation of computers used integrated circuits (ICs)?
questions.explanation: Third-generation computers (1965-1971) used integrated circuits.

questions.text: What is the function of an operating system?
questions.explanation: An operating system acts as an interface between user and hardware, managing resources.

questions.text: What is the value or meaning of the full form of USB in mathematics?
questions.explanation: USB stands for Universal Serial Bus, used for connecting peripherals.

questions.text: Which of the following is an example of system software?
questions.explanation: Windows 10 is an operating system, which is system software.

questions.text: What is the meaning of "the purpose of a firewall"?
questions.explanation: A firewall monitors and controls incoming and outgoing network traffic for security.

questions.text: Which device converts digital signals to analogue for transmission over phone lines?
questions.explanation: A modulator-demodulator (modem) converts digital signals to analogue and vice versa.

questions.text: What is the value or meaning of a spreadsheet used for in mathematics?
options: Organising and calculating data in rows and columns
questions.explanation: A spreadsheet application is used to enter, manipulate, and calculate numerical data.

questions.text: Which of the following produces hard copies of documents?
questions.explanation: A printer produces physical (hard) copies of digital documents.

questions.text: What is the hexadecimal equivalent of decimal 15?
questions.explanation: In hexadecimal, decimal 15 is represented as F.

questions.text: What does the acronym SQL stand for?
questions.explanation: SQL stands for Structured Query Language, used for managing databases.

questions.text: Which top-level domain is commonly used for educational institutions?
questions.explanation: The .edu domain is reserved for educational institutions.

questions.text: What is the purpose of an assembler?
options: Translate assembly language to machine code
questions.explanation: An assembler translates assembly language programs into machine code.

questions.text: Which of the following is a valid variable name in BASIC?
questions.explanation: Variable names must start with a letter; NAME$ is valid for a string variable.

questions.text: What is the role of the ALU in a CPU?
questions.explanation: The Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU) performs all arithmetic and logical operations.

questions.text: What does the control unit of a CPU do?
options: Directs and coordinates all CPU operations
questions.explanation: The control unit fetches, decodes, and directs the execution of instructions.

questions.text: What is the value or meaning of virtual memory in mathematics?
options: An illusion of additional RAM using disk space
questions.explanation: Virtual memory uses a portion of the hard disk to simulate additional RAM.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a logic gate?
questions.explanation: ADD is an arithmetic operation, not a logic gate.

questions.text: What is the output of a NOT gate when the input is 1?
questions.explanation: A NOT gate inverts the input, so input 1 produces output 0.

questions.text: What does the booting process of a computer involve?
options: Loading the operating system into RAM
questions.explanation: Booting loads the operating system from storage into RAM so the computer can operate.

questions.text: What is a presentation software used for?
questions.explanation: Presentation software like PowerPoint is used to create visual slide presentations.

questions.text: What does the acronym FTP stand for?
questions.explanation: FTP stands for File Transfer Protocol, used for transferring files between computers.

questions.text: What is the difference between ROM and RAM?
options: ROM is non-volatile; RAM is volatile
questions.explanation: ROM retains data without power (non-volatile), while RAM loses data when power is off (volatile).

questions.text: Which device is used to connect multiple networks together?
questions.explanation: A router forwards data packets between different networks.

questions.text: What is the purpose of a database management system (DBMS)?
questions.explanation: A DBMS is software that allows users to create, retrieve, update, and manage data in databases.

questions.text: What does the computing term GUI stand for?
questions.explanation: GUI stands for Graphical User Interface, which allows users to interact with visual elements.

questions.text: What is the binary equivalent of the hexadecimal digit A?
questions.explanation: Hexadecimal A equals 10 in decimal, which is 1010 in binary.

questions.text: What is the value or meaning of an IPO chart used for in mathematics?
options: Showing Input, Process, and Output of a system
questions.explanation: An IPO (Input-Process-Output) chart describes the data flow of a system.

questions.text: Which of the following is an example of cloud computing?
options: Saving files to a local hard disk
Using Google Drive to store files online
questions.explanation: Google Drive provides cloud storage, allowing access to files over the Internet.

questions.text: What is the value or meaning of the full meaning of AI in mathematics?
questions.explanation: AI stands for Artificial Intelligence, the simulation of human intelligence by machines.

questions.text: What is the value or meaning of e-waste in mathematics?
questions.explanation: E-waste refers to discarded electrical and electronic equipment.

questions.text: Which of the following is a blogging platform?
questions.explanation: WordPress is a popular platform for creating and managing blogs and websites.

questions.text: What is the value or meaning of phishing in mathematics?
options: A fraudulent attempt to obtain sensitive information by pretending to be trustworthy
questions.explanation: Phishing is a cyber attack where attackers impersonate legitimate entities to steal personal data.

questions.text: What does the term 'bandwidth' refer to?
options: The maximum rate of data transfer across a network
The number of users on a network
questions.explanation: Bandwidth measures the maximum amount of data that can be transmitted per unit time.

questions.text: What is the purpose of a search engine?
options: Search and retrieve information from the web
questions.explanation: A search engine indexes web content and helps users find relevant information online.

questions.text: Which programming language is commonly used for web page design?
questions.explanation: HTML (HyperText Markup Language) is used to structure and design web pages.

questions.text: What is the function of a proxy server?
options: Act as an intermediary between client and the Internet
questions.explanation: A proxy server acts as an intermediary, forwarding requests from clients to the Internet.

questions.text: What is the octal equivalent of decimal 8?
questions.explanation: Decimal 8 equals 10 in octal (1Ã—8 + 0Ã—1).

questions.text: What is the meaning of "the purpose of a trackball"?
options: Pointing device that operates by rolling a ball
questions.explanation: A trackball is a pointing device where the user rolls a ball to control the cursor.

questions.text: What is the value or meaning of machine language in mathematics?
options: Binary code (0s and 1s) directly understood by the computer
questions.explanation: Machine language is the lowest-level language consisting of binary digits (0s and 1s).

questions.text: Which of the following is a measure of computer speed?
questions.explanation: CPU speed is measured in Hertz (Hz), e.g., GHz (gigahertz).

questions.text: What does the acronym IoT stand for?
questions.explanation: IoT stands for Internet of Things, a network of interconnected smart devices.

questions.text: What is an IPO in the context of computing?
questions.explanation: IPO stands for Input, Process, Output, describing how data flows through a system.

questions.text: Which type of memory has the fastest access time?
questions.explanation: Cache memory is the fastest memory, located closest to the CPU.

questions.text: What is an Ethernet cable primarily used for?
questions.explanation: An Ethernet cable provides a wired connection to a local area network (LAN).

questions.text: What is the main advantage of optical fibre over copper cable?
options: Higher data transmission speed and less signal loss
questions.explanation: Optical fibre transmits data as light, offering higher speeds and less signal attenuation.

questions.text: What is the decimal equivalent of hexadecimal 1A?
questions.explanation: Hex 1A = 1Ã—16 + 10 = 26 in decimal.

questions.text: What does the PRINT statement do in BASIC?
questions.explanation: The PRINT statement outputs text or values to the screen.

questions.text: What is the value or meaning of a character set in mathematics?
options: A collection of letters, digits, and symbols the computer recognises
questions.explanation: A character set is the complete set of characters that a computer can represent.

questions.text: What does the acronym ASCII stand for in full?
options: American Standard Code for Information Interchange
Advanced System Code for Integrated Intelligence
Applied Science Code for Internal Exchange
questions.explanation: ASCII stands for American Standard Code for Information Interchange, a character encoding standard.

questions.text: What is the output of an XOR gate when both inputs are the same?
questions.explanation: An XOR gate outputs 0 when both inputs are the same (both 0 or both 1).

questions.text: What is the purpose of a trackpad on a laptop?
options: Move the cursor and interact with the screen
questions.explanation: A trackpad is a pointing device built into laptops, replacing a mouse.

questions.text: What is the value or meaning of the full form of PDF in mathematics?
questions.explanation: PDF stands for Portable Document Format, developed by Adobe for document sharing.

questions.text: What is the difference between a switch and a hub?
options: A switch sends data only to the intended port; a hub broadcasts to all
questions.explanation: A switch intelligently directs data to the target device, while a hub broadcasts to all ports.

questions.text: Which of the following is a benefit of using ICT in education?
options: Provides access to vast online learning resources
questions.explanation: ICT provides learners with access to e-learning materials, simulations, and global resources.

questions.text: What is the value or meaning of a peripheral device in mathematics?
options: A device that connects to the computer to extend its capabilities
questions.explanation: A peripheral is an auxiliary device like a printer, mouse, or keyboard connected to the computer.

questions.text: What does the command FOR...NEXT do in BASIC?
options: Creates a loop that repeats a block of code
questions.explanation: FOR...NEXT creates a counted loop, executing code a specified number of times.

questions.text: What is the binary equivalent of the octal number 7?
questions.explanation: Octal 7 equals 7 in decimal, which is 111 in binary.

questions.text: What is a star topology's main disadvantage?
options: If the central hub fails, the whole network fails
questions.explanation: Star topology depends on the central hub; its failure brings down the entire network.

questions.text: What is the primary role of an antivirus program?
questions.explanation: An antivirus program scans for, detects, and removes malware and viruses.

questions.text: What is the function of the recycle bin on a computer desktop?
options: Temporarily stores deleted files for possible recovery
questions.explanation: The recycle bin holds deleted files temporarily, allowing restoration before permanent deletion.

questions.text: What does MAN stand for in networking?
questions.explanation: MAN stands for Metropolitan Area Network, connecting users across a city or campus.

questions.text: What is the decimal equivalent of binary 10000?
questions.explanation: Binary 10000 = 1Ã—2^4 = 16 in decimal.

questions.text: What is the value or meaning of a compiler in mathematics?
options: An interpreter that reads code line by line
A program that translates the entire source code into machine code at once
questions.explanation: A compiler translates the whole high-level source program into machine code before execution.

questions.text: What is a key difference between a compiler and an interpreter?
options: A compiler translates all at once; an interpreter translates line by line during execution
questions.explanation: A compiler translates the entire program upfront, while an interpreter translates and executes one line at a time.

questions.text: What is the main purpose of a word processor?
options: Creating, editing, and formatting text documents
questions.explanation: A word processor is application software for writing, editing, and formatting text.

questions.text: Which protocol is used to view web pages?
questions.explanation: HTTP (HyperText Transfer Protocol) and its secure version HTTPS are used to access web pages.

questions.text: What is the value or meaning of the full meaning of VPN in mathematics?
questions.explanation: VPN stands for Virtual Private Network, which creates a secure encrypted connection over the Internet.

questions.text: What is the main feature of blockchain technology?
questions.explanation: Blockchain is a decentralised, distributed ledger where transactions are recorded immutably.

questions.text: Which generation of computers used microprocessors?

questions.text: What is the function of a light pen?

questions.explanation: A light pen is a pointing device that detects light from a CRT monitor to select screen positions.

questions.text: What is the value or meaning of the purpose of the DNS in mathematics?
options: Translate domain names to IP addresses
questions.explanation: DNS (Domain Name System) translates human-readable domain names into IP addresses.

questions.text: What is the function of OCR technology?
options: Convert printed or handwritten text into machine-readable data
questions.explanation: OCR (Optical Character Recognition) scans text images and converts them into editable digital text.

questions.text: What is the value or meaning of an SSD in mathematics?
options: A solid-state drive with no moving parts for data storage
questions.explanation: An SSD (Solid State Drive) uses flash memory for faster, more reliable data storage than HDDs.

questions.text: What is the difference between the Internet and the World Wide Web?
options: The Internet is the infrastructure; the Web is a service running on it
The Web came before the Internet
The Internet is for emails only
questions.explanation: The Internet is the global network infrastructure, while the WWW is an information system using it.

questions.text: What does the IF...THEN statement do in programming?
options: Executes a block of code only if a condition is true
questions.explanation: IF...THEN is a conditional structure that executes code only when the specified condition is true.

questions.text: What is the value or meaning of the purpose of a UPS in mathematics?
options: Provide temporary power during an outage to protect the computer
questions.explanation: A UPS (Uninterruptible Power Supply) provides backup power to keep a computer running during power cuts.

questions.text: What is the purpose of a barcode reader?
options: Scan and decode barcodes into data for the computer
questions.explanation: A barcode reader scans barcodes and converts them into digital data for processing.

questions.text: What is the value or meaning of a macro in a spreadsheet in mathematics?
options: A recorded sequence of actions that can be replayed automatically
questions.explanation: A macro automates repetitive tasks by recording a sequence of user actions.

questions.text: What is the function of a decompiler?
options: Convert machine code back into a higher-level language
questions.explanation: A decompiler attempts to reverse machine code into a more readable high-level language.

questions.text: What is the purpose of a crash in computing?
options: A sudden failure where a program or the OS stops functioning properly
questions.explanation: A crash is an unexpected stop of a program or operating system due to errors.

questions.text: Which of the following is an example of wearable technology?
questions.explanation: A smartwatch is wearable technology worn on the body that performs computing functions.

questions.text: What is the main advantage of open-source software?
options: Always free and can be modified by users
Only runs on one operating system
questions.explanation: Open-source software allows users to view, modify, and distribute the source code freely.

questions.text: What does the acronym ERP stand for?
questions.explanation: ERP stands for Enterprise Resource Planning, software for managing core business processes.

questions.text: What is meant by the term 'malware'?
options: Malicious software designed to harm a computer system
questions.explanation: Malware is any software intentionally designed to cause damage to computers or networks.

questions.text: What is the value or meaning of the full form of Wi-Fi in mathematics?
questions.explanation: Wi-Fi is commonly understood as Wireless Fidelity, a technology for wireless networking.

questions.text: What is the function of the operating system file manager?
options: Organise, store, retrieve, and manage files and folders
questions.explanation: The file manager allows users to create, rename, move, delete, and organise files and directories.

questions.text: What is the meaning of "the purpose of data backup"?
options: Create copies of data to restore in case of loss or damage
questions.explanation: Backing up data ensures copies exist to recover from hardware failure, theft, or accidental deletion.

questions.text: What is the purpose of a primary key in a database?
options: Uniquely identify each record in a table
questions.explanation: A primary key uniquely identifies each record in a database table, ensuring no duplicates.

questions.text: Which of the following is a type of computer network cable?
questions.explanation: Cat5 and Cat6 are twisted-pair Ethernet cables commonly used for LAN connections.

questions.text: What is the value or meaning of a cookie on a website in mathematics?
options: A small file stored on a user's browser by a website to remember data
questions.explanation: A cookie is a small text file placed on a user's device by a website to store preferences and session data.

questions.text: What is the main purpose of e-commerce?
options: Buy and sell goods and services over the Internet
questions.explanation: E-commerce enables buying and selling of products and services through online platforms.

questions.text: What is the main purpose of 5G technology?
options: Provide faster and more reliable wireless communication
questions.explanation: 5G is the fifth generation of mobile network technology offering higher speeds and lower latency.

questions.text: What is the function of a light-emitting diode (LED) indicator on a device?
options: Provide a visual status signal (power, activity, etc.)
questions.explanation: LED indicators give visual feedback about the status of a device, such as power on or data transfer.

questions.text: What is the value or meaning of a domain name in mathematics?
options: A human-readable address that identifies a website on the Internet
questions.explanation: A domain name (e.g., www.example.com) is a human-friendly address for a website, mapped to an IP via DNS.

questions.text: Which of the following is a property of RAM?
options: Volatile and used for temporary data storage
questions.explanation: RAM is volatile memory that temporarily stores data and instructions currently in use by the CPU.

questions.text: What does the term 'network topology' describe?
options: The physical or logical arrangement of devices in a network
questions.explanation: Network topology refers to the layout and arrangement of various elements (nodes, links) in a network.

questions.text: What is the difference between RAM and ROM?
options: RAM is permanent, ROM is temporary
RAM is volatile, ROM is non-volatile
questions.explanation: RAM is volatile (loses data without power), while ROM is non-volatile (retains data without power).

questions.text: What is the meaning of "the function of a plotter"?
options: Produce large-format high-quality prints and engineering drawings
questions.explanation: A plotter is an output device that produces vector graphics on large sheets of paper.

questions.text: What does the term 'cloud computing' mean?
options: Delivery of computing services (storage, processing) over the Internet
questions.explanation: Cloud computing provides on-demand computing resources like storage and processing over the Internet.

questions.text: What is the decimal equivalent of binary 111?
questions.explanation: Binary 111 = 4+2+1 = 7 in decimal.

questions.text: What is the function of an operating system scheduler?
options: Allocate CPU time to different processes
questions.explanation: The OS scheduler determines which process gets CPU time and for how long.

questions.text: What is the value or meaning of an Ethernet frame in mathematics?
options: A structured unit of data transmitted over an Ethernet network
questions.explanation: An Ethernet frame is the data unit (packet format) used to transmit data over Ethernet networks.

questions.text: What is the meaning of "the purpose of encryption"?
options: Convert data into a coded form to prevent unauthorised access
questions.explanation: Encryption converts readable data into an unreadable format to protect it from unauthorised access.

questions.text: Which generation of computers used vacuum tubes?
questions.explanation: First-generation computers (1940-1956) used vacuum tubes as their main electronic component.

questions.text: What does a programmer use a flowchart for?
options: Visually represent the logic and steps of a program
questions.explanation: A flowchart uses standard symbols to visually represent the sequence of steps in a program.

questions.text: What is the primary advantage of using a tablet computer?
questions.explanation: Tablets are lightweight, portable devices with touchscreens for easy mobile computing.

questions.text: What is a satellite connection used for in ICT?
options: Communication and data transmission via orbiting satellites
questions.explanation: Satellite connections transmit and receive data through satellites orbiting the Earth.

questions.text: What does the term 'node' mean in networking?
options: Any device connected to a network that can send, receive, or forward data
questions.explanation: A node is any device (computer, printer, router) connected to a network that can communicate.

questions.text: What is the octal equivalent of decimal 9?

questions.text: What is the function of a sound card?
options: Process and output audio signals to speakers or headphones
questions.explanation: A sound card processes audio data for input (microphone) and output (speakers/headphones).

questions.text: What does the term 'cybersecurity' refer to?
options: The practice of protecting computer systems and networks from digital attacks
questions.explanation: Cybersecurity involves protecting systems, networks, and data from digital attacks and unauthorised access.

questions.text: What is the main function of the motherboard?
options: Connect and allow communication between all hardware components
questions.explanation: The motherboard is the main circuit board that connects the CPU, RAM, storage, and peripherals.

questions.text: What is the function of the BIOS during startup?

questions.text: Which of the following is a characteristic of the third generation of computers?

questions.text: What is the value or meaning of a web browser in mathematics?
options: Software used to access and view websites on the Internet
questions.explanation: A web browser (e.g., Chrome, Firefox) retrieves and displays web pages from the Internet.

questions.text: What is the purpose of a computer port?
options: A connection point for external devices to communicate with the computer
questions.explanation: Ports (USB, HDMI, serial, etc.) are interfaces for connecting peripheral devices to a computer.

questions.text: What is the value or meaning of the full meaning of LAN in mathematics?
questions.explanation: LAN stands for Local Area Network, a network covering a small geographical area like a building.

questions.text: What does the DIM command do in BASIC?

questions.explanation: The DIM statement in BASIC is used to declare arrays and allocate storage for them.

questions.text: What is the full meaning of the acronym ISP?
questions.explanation: ISP stands for Internet Service Provider, the company that gives you access to the Internet.

questions.text: What is the difference between application software and system software?
options: System software is for users; application software manages hardware
Application software performs specific tasks; system software manages hardware and runs the computer
questions.explanation: System software (OS, drivers) manages hardware; application software (Word, Excel) performs user tasks.

questions.text: What is the purpose of a disk defragmenter?
options: Reorganise fragmented data on a hard disk to improve access speed
questions.explanation: Defragmentation rearranges data on an HDD so files are stored contiguously, improving read speed.

questions.text: What is the hexadecimal equivalent of decimal 31?

questions.text: What is the value or meaning of a client-server network in mathematics?

questions.explanation: In a client-server model, a central server manages resources and services requested by client machines.

questions.text: What is the purpose of OCR software?
options: Convert images of printed or handwritten text into editable text
questions.explanation: OCR (Optical Character Recognition) reads text from scanned images and converts it into editable data.

questions.text: What is the role of a motherboard chipset?

questions.explanation: The chipset controls communication between the processor, memory, and other hardware components.

questions.text: What does the term 'interface' mean in computing?
options: A point of interaction between two systems or a user and a computer
questions.explanation: An interface is the shared boundary where two components, systems, or users interact.

questions.text: What is the binary equivalent of decimal 5?

questions.text: What is the best definition of a variable in programming?
options: A named storage location that holds data which can change during execution
questions.explanation: A variable is a named memory location whose value can be assigned and modified during program execution.

questions.text: What is the purpose of a dummy value in a loop?
options: A counter variable that controls the number of loop iterations
questions.explanation: A dummy or counter variable controls how many times a loop executes.

questions.text: What is a peephole optimization in compilers?
options: Looking through a hole in the monitor
A technique to improve code by optimising small sequences of instructions
questions.explanation: Peephole optimization examines and improves a short sequence of generated instructions.

questions.text: What is the value or meaning of an IP address in mathematics?
options: A physical address of a building
A unique numerical label assigned to each device on a network
questions.explanation: An IP address uniquely identifies a device on a network, enabling communication (e.g., 192.168.1.1).

questions.text: What is the main function of a CPU register?
options: Hold data temporarily for immediate processing by the ALU
questions.explanation: Registers are small, ultra-fast storage locations inside the CPU used for immediate data operations.

questions.text: In networking, what does a topology diagram show about a network?
options: The physical or logical layout of a computer network
questions.explanation: A network topology diagram illustrates how devices and cables are arranged in a network.

questions.text: What is the meaning of "meant by 'data redundancy'"?
options: Unnecessary duplication of the same data in multiple places
questions.explanation: Data redundancy occurs when the same data is unnecessarily duplicated across multiple locations.

questions.text: What is the purpose of a data dictionary in a DBMS?
options: Store metadata describing the structure, types, and constraints of data
questions.explanation: A data dictionary stores metadata (definitions, types, constraints) about the database structure.

questions.text: What is peer-to-peer (P2P) networking?
options: All computers share resources equally with no central server
A single computer with no network
questions.explanation: In P2P networking, all computers are equal and can share files and resources without a central server.

questions.text: What is the main purpose of the WHILE...WEND loop in BASIC?
options: Repeat a block of code as long as a condition remains true
questions.explanation: WHILE...WEND repeatedly executes a block of code as long as the specified condition is true.

questions.text: What does an operating system do during multitasking?
options: Runs only one program at a time
Rapidly switches between multiple programs to give the illusion of simultaneous execution
questions.explanation: Multitasking allows the OS to rapidly switch CPU time among multiple programs, appearing to run them simultaneously.

questions.text: What is the value or meaning of a supercomputer in mathematics?
options: The fastest type of computer used for complex calculations and large-scale processing
questions.explanation: Supercomputers are the most powerful computers, used for weather forecasting, nuclear simulations, etc.

questions.text: What is the value or meaning of a smart card in mathematics?
options: A plastic card with an embedded microchip for identification or payment
questions.explanation: A smart card has an embedded chip used for secure identification, authentication, and data storage.

questions.text: What is the main disadvantage of using public Wi-Fi?
options: It is less secure and more vulnerable to data interception
questions.explanation: Public Wi-Fi networks are less secure, making it easier for attackers to intercept data.

questions.text: What does a cursor represent on a computer screen?
options: A visual indicator showing the current position for text input or pointing
questions.explanation: A cursor is a movable indicator on screen showing where input will appear or where a click will occur.

questions.text: What is the decimal equivalent of hexadecimal FF?
questions.explanation: Hex FF = 15Ã—16 + 15 = 240+15 = 255 in decimal.

questions.text: What is the purpose of a capacitor on a motherboard?
options: Store and release small amounts of electrical charge to stabilise voltage
questions.explanation: Capacitors smooth out voltage fluctuations and provide stable power to components on the motherboard.

questions.text: What is the purpose of a taskbar in an operating system?
options: Show running applications and allow quick switching between windows
questions.explanation: The taskbar displays open programs and system icons, allowing users to switch between applications.

questions.text: What does the term 'latency' mean in networking?
options: The delay before data begins to transfer after a request
questions.explanation: Latency is the time delay between sending a request and receiving a response over a network.

questions.text: What is the value or meaning of an epoch in computing in mathematics?
options: A fixed point in time used as a reference for timekeeping in computers
questions.explanation: An epoch is a reference point (e.g., Jan 1, 1970 in Unix time) from which system time is calculated.

questions.text: What is the primary function of an Operating System Kernel?
options: Manage core system resources including memory, CPU scheduling, and I/O
questions.explanation: The kernel is the core of an OS that manages hardware resources, process scheduling, and memory.

questions.text: What is a Boolean value in programming?
options: A data type that can only be TRUE or FALSE
questions.explanation: A Boolean data type represents one of two values: TRUE or FALSE.

questions.text: What does the ternary operator allow in a programming language?
options: A shorthand way to write an if-else statement in a single line
questions.explanation: The ternary operator is a compact conditional expression: condition ? value_if_true : value_if_false.

questions.text: What is the meaning of "the full meaning of EEPROM"?
questions.explanation: EEPROM is non-volatile memory that can be erased and reprogrammed electrically.

questions.text: What is the purpose of a barcode system in a library?
options: Track and manage the borrowing and returning of books
questions.explanation: Barcode systems in libraries track which books are borrowed, returned, and their locations.

questions.text: What is the main role of the World Wide Web Consortium (W3C)?
options: Develop web standards to ensure long-term growth of the web
questions.explanation: W3C develops standards and guidelines to ensure the long-term growth and interoperability of the web.

questions.text: What is a hexadecimal colour code in web design?
options: A 6-digit code preceded by # representing RGB colour values
questions.explanation: A hex colour code (e.g., #FF5733) represents RGB values using hexadecimal digits.

questions.text: What is a mainframe computer typically used for?
options: Large-scale enterprise computing such as banking and government transactions
questions.explanation: Mainframes handle massive data processing for banks, airlines, and government systems.

questions.text: What is the value or meaning of a protocol in networking in mathematics?
options: A set of rules that govern data communication between devices
questions.explanation: Protocols define the rules and standards for how data is transmitted and received over a network.

questions.text: What does the term 'hacktivism' mean?
options: Using hacking skills to promote a political or social cause
questions.explanation: Hacktivism is the use of hacking techniques to advance a political or social agenda.

questions.text: What is the purpose of RAM in a computer?
options: Provide temporary, fast-access storage for data and instructions currently in use
questions.explanation: RAM temporarily holds data and instructions that the CPU needs quick access to during processing.

questions.text: What is the meaning of "the main function of a CPU"?
options: Fetch, decode, and execute instructions to process data
questions.explanation: The CPU fetches instructions from memory, decodes them, and executes them to process data.
